title: Faker Island. Profiling misinformation sharers on the French Twittersphere using a matching procedure
screen_reason: Observational Twitter study of the French Twittersphere (184 million tweets containing a URL to one of 420 French media outlets, 3.7 million accounts, May 2018 - May 2020). Misinformation is defined at URL level: articles independently rated false or misleading by fact-checkers (Les Decodeurs/Decodex and the Facebook-Social Science One third-party fact-check database), 1,548 such URLs. The paper reports two observed sharing shares with explicit denominators: 0.05% of the 184M tweets contained at least one misinformation item, and 0.9% of the 3.7M accounts shared at least one. The rest of the paper (matched comparison of 1,907 sharers with 958 ideologically comparable controls) is a profiling analysis, not prevalence.

estimates.measure_type: % of tweets linking to French media outlets that contained at least one fact-checked misinformation URL
estimates.denominator: 184 million tweets containing a URL pointing to one of 420 prominent French media outlets, posted by 3.7 million accounts between May 2018 and May 2020
estimates.definition: Tweet contained at least one of the 1,548 URLs from those 420 outlets that had been labelled misinformation by fact-checkers in the Decodex database or the Facebook Privacy Protected Shared URLs database
estimates.misinfo_def: misinformation is defined as the sharing of specific URLs corresponding to individual articles that were independently evaluated as false or misleading by fact-checkers
estimates.source_quote: We were then able to identify around 85K tweets (i.e., 0.05% of the initial 184M) containing at least one misinformation item and around 31.5K accounts that had shared them (i.e., 0.9% of the initial 3.7 M).
estimates.page_loc: Section 2.1 Identification of misinformation sharers, p. 8-9
estimates.ground_truth_detail: URL-level fact-check labels from Les Decodeurs (Le Monde, Decodex) and the Facebook Privacy Protected Shared URLs database via Social Science One, whose French third-party fact-checkers are AFP Factuel, Les Decodeurs, Les Observateurs (France 24) and Fake Off (20 Minutes); labels include 'false' and 'mixture or false headline'. The authors state explicitly that outlets are not classified as misinformation websites; only individual articles are.
estimates.moderator_quote: This dataset was built by a team of researchers who, starting from a curated list of 420 prominent French media outlets, then collected every tweet containing a URL pointing to any of those 420 media websites by relying on the open-source Gazouilloire tool
estimates.notes: Denominator is tweets carrying a French-media URL, not all French tweets, so this is a share of media-link sharing rather than of all platform content; coded news_diet + curated for that reason. Year given as the midpoint of the May 2018 - May 2020 collection window. The authors warn the figure is a lower bound because fact-checkers cannot assess everything, and simultaneously an upper bound relative to the whole platform because lurkers are excluded from the frame.

estimates.measure_type: % of accounts in the French Twittersphere dataset that shared at least one fact-checked misinformation URL
estimates.value_raw: around 31.5K accounts that had shared them (i.e., 0.9% of the initial 3.7 M)
estimates.denominator: 3.7 million unique Twitter accounts that posted at least one tweet containing a URL to one of 420 French media outlets, May 2018 - May 2020
estimates.definition: Account shared at least one of the 1,548 URLs labelled misinformation by fact-checkers
estimates.misinfo_def: misinformation is defined as the sharing of specific URLs corresponding to individual articles that were independently evaluated as false or misleading by fact-checkers
estimates.source_quote: We were then able to identify around 85K tweets (i.e., 0.05% of the initial 184M) containing at least one misinformation item and around 31.5K accounts that had shared them (i.e., 0.9% of the initial 3.7 M).
estimates.page_loc: Section 2.1 Identification of misinformation sharers, p. 8-9
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same URL-level fact-check labels (Decodex; Facebook/Social Science One third-party fact-checks). Account is counted once for sharing at least one flagged URL.
estimates.moderator_quote: This collection process yielded over 184 million tweets posted by 3.7 million unique user accounts between May 2018 and May 2020
estimates.notes: Denominator is accounts, not content: this is the share of USERS who ever shared a flagged URL, distinct from the 0.05% of tweets in the row above. The user population is itself selected (only accounts that tweeted a French media link), which the authors say inflates the rate relative to all French Twitter users; they add 'we cannot state with certainty that the exact prevalence of misinformation disseminators on the French Twittersphere is 0.9% of users'. Elsewhere the paper gives the count as 31,760 rather than 31.5K.

missed_or_uncertain: Deliberately not extracted. (1) 'most users (over 90 %) shared fewer than five items, and only 0.02 % shared more than 50' - a distribution of sharing intensity among sharers, not a top-X%-account-for-Y%-of-activity pair, so it fails the CONCENTRATION rule requiring both a group share and an activity share. The paper asserts concentration ('misinformation sharing on the French Twittersphere is concentrated within a small minority of users') without ever quantifying the activity share, which is a genuine gap given RQ1 asks about concentration. (2) The distribution of the 1,548 flagged URLs across outlet types (66% counter-information, 18% partisan, 9% mainstream, 8% peripheral) - a within-misinformation source breakdown, not a prevalence share, and the authors state these categories are structural hyperlink clusters and 'not fact-checking labels'. (3) The share of tweets linking to counter-informational media (15% for sharers vs 8% for controls, Table 1) - tempting as an unreliable-source share, but counter-information here is a hyperlink-cluster category with no veracity ground truth, so it is not a misinformation measure. (4) '10,910 accounts, representing just over 30%' of the 31,760 sharers locatable in the ideological space, and '8.6% of the 3.7M users' mapped - coverage rates of the ideological inference, not misinformation shares. (5) All matched-comparison percentages (42.1% vs 19.4% political markers in bios; 92% vs 34% hyperactivity; 23% vs 41% original tweets; 72% vs 52% retweets; engagement rates) - profiling contrasts between sharers and controls, not prevalence. (6) Supplementary Table 1 reproduces headline figures from other studies (Gaumont et al. 0.081%; Grinberg et al. 1% of users exposed to 80% of fake news; Osmundsen et al. 11%; Baribi-Bartov et al. 2,107 supersharers = 80%) - figures cited from elsewhere, excluded by rule. Note on the text: this is a working manuscript containing three alternative abstracts, an internal note headed 'Proposition Sacha', and two differently worded RQ1 and RQ2 statements; the numbers in the methods and results are consistent across them, but a reader should be aware the file is a draft, not a published version.

rob.design: Observational digital-trace study. Frame: 184M tweets carrying a URL to one of 420 curated French media outlets, 3.7M accounts, May 2018 - May 2020, collected with Gazouilloire via the Twitter streaming and search APIs (Cardon et al. 2019; Cointet et al. 2021b). Misinformation identified at URL level from two fact-check databases (1,548 flagged URLs), giving ~85K tweets and ~31.5K sharing accounts. Ideological positions inferred from MP-following patterns in a validated latent space covering 368,831 French users; 10,910 of the sharers (30%) could be placed. Profiling uses a matching procedure comparing 1,907 sharers with 958 ideologically comparable controls. Manual coding tasks in the paper report percentage agreement 89-90% and kappa 0.780 and 0.801. No response rate applies; the main threats are the restrictive definition of the Twittersphere and the incompleteness of fact-check coverage, both acknowledged.
